It’s lively in the club. The room is blasting with music that pounds her ears, the DJ hypes up the crowd with songs that they know everyone will shake their ass to. She looks down from the VIP section where her college friend takes the group because it’s her birthday, and the drinks keep on coming—some from a group of guys from another table, which they all take with barely disguised repulsion. Free alcohol is free alcohol after all. Relatively, it’s an enjoyable night.

Phainon had always considered herself to be a party girl. Not because she likes the environment—far from it, as she hates loud noises—but she likes having a good time with her friends in outfits she would never wear in a normal setting. She loves to show off some dance moves her friends would never expect she’s capable of while feeling a little buzzed. She loves playing drinking games with the girls even though she’s not too big on alcohol.

Another thing is that she also loves it when her friends hype her up to talk to a girl she finds attractive. Only, the magic disappears the moment she’s there. Because her heart is just never in it—at least not for the past two months. And she knows exactly why that is.

All those reasons for loving parties might be fun, cute even. But one ugly reason for always going to parties in every chance she gets is that she always seeks a distraction. Not from her studies, oh Titans, no. She passes her courses with no problem. Even if she doesn’t excel in every single one of them, she takes no issue with it. She always finds studying too hard to be sucking the life out of a person. What can she say? A healthy life leads to a healthy mind.

No, the one thing she always runs away from is her dorm room. Specifically, her roommate, Mydei. They’ve been roommates for over a year now, so they’re quite close already. Mydei had always cooked both of them dinner, especially when they came home at the same time—then Phainon would assist her a little. Phainon took care of other chores such as laundry and dishwashing. They have a balanced allocation of chores, so they never argue in that regard. Oftentimes, they do bicker, but it’s not unusual in their relationship. Sometimes, they get a little too close for normal, though none of them think to address it. So all in all, they’re chill.

But one day, two months ago, Mydei brought in a girl. She claims it’s her friend, but Phainon has never even met her before. More importantly, Mydei doesn’t bring anyone home. She’s always the one to stay in her friends’ place to hang out. Phainon thought they’re in silent agreement about not bringing anyone in, as their dorm room is their own sacred space, and she doesn’t bring anyone in either. But apparently, Phainon’s the only one who thinks so. And ever since that day, she and Mydei barely talk—or at least, she barely talks to Mydei—they only do so when it’s about rent and utilities, or when it’s time to eat dinner. Which Phainon also tries to avoid more lately.

Each time she senses Mydei would try to talk to her about it—when she looks at Phainon with a worried and dejected look on her face, though it’s subtle—she dresses up and heads out. She doesn’t want to hear it.

“Where are you going?” Mydei would ask the next evening. “Dinner’s almost done.”

“Yeah sorry. Cipher invited me over,” Phainon would say on a whim. In reality, she had never stepped foot in Cipher's dorm room. Both of them had always hung out in Hyacine’s place.

From then on, Mydei stopped making dinner for both of them.

Phainon knows she’s being petty. Mydei didn’t even do anything wrong, because they never even spoke about the supposed agreement. But the thing is, that day made her realize something. The sinking feeling in her stomach, the ugliness and bitterness of it, they were all for a reason. Mydei bringing someone over so suddenly wasn’t the issue for Phainon—she would’ve felt something regardless. No, the issue was that Mydei brought someone over, period. There’s only one word to describe that ugly feeling: jealousy.

(What she doesn’t know is that Mydei never brought someone over again ever since that day.)

And it is, indeed, as what they say—ugly. She never even went out to see them together in the dorms. She would wait until she’s alone to go out and take something from the fridge to eat. And since it was a weekend that time, she didn’t have to go out to attend classes. Suddenly, she finds solitude in her own room. When on a normal day, she’d die if she had to stay there for more than three hours. The AC in her room hasn’t been working for a while, and the summer heat was becoming crazier by the day.

No one has to know how she cried silently for a few hours that day, though.

“Hey Phai,” one of the girls from the group calls out to her. “When are you ever gonna introduce us to your hot roommate?”

Another adds on, “Yeah! All we got was that picture you showed us a long time ago. You never talked about her again. Tell me,” the girl leans closer in intrigue, placing her chin on her palm as she rests her elbow on the table. “Is she single?”

Looking at her drink, contemplating about getting another round but deciding against it, Phainon tries to shift to another topic by dropping this one. “No, she isn’t,” she says definitively, the lie coming out too naturally. When she thinks about it, it’s technically not even a lie, is it?

Phainon tunes out the group as they continue their celebration for the rest of the night. She tells one of the girls she’ll head down in hopes of enjoying herself with a girl from the dance floor, just so they don’t worry. But she makes a turn to the exit instead and hangs by the alley. The cool evening breeze hits her skin as she leans onto the wall and she pulls out her box of cigarettes. She takes a stick and puts the filter on her mouth, not quite lighting it. She promised Mydei she’d quit.

The exit door opens before her, catching her attention. She finds that the person behind it is none other than Cipher, who came with her to the party. Of course she would follow Phainon. She definitely sensed there was something wrong when Mydei was brought up. Phainon never even told her about their situation, nor her recent… realization.

“Smoking again, huh?” she says teasingly, crossing her arms as she leans beside Phainon. “I thought you quit.”

“I am,” Phainon says without looking at her, fiddling with the box in her hands. “I’m not lighting it.”

“Still keeping true to your word even after your little catfight?”

Phainon blushes, her face heating up, almost overriding the breeze. But she still doesn’t turn to look at her, afraid of what her own eyes might convey. “I don’t know what you’re talking about.”

Cipher raises an eyebrow. “You really think I wouldn’t know?”

The cigarette filter almost rips from being bitten into a little too harshly, Phainon’s jaw tensing by the minute. “Still don’t know what you’re talking about.”

The girl sighs beside her, defeated. “Your roomie texted to ask if you’ve been eating well.”

Now, Phainon was finally looking at her, wide-eyed. “You’re lying.”

“I wish I was. Then I wouldn’t be caught in the middle of… whatever the fuck is going on between you two,” she meets her eyes with a flash of annoyance, but Phainon knows not to take it to heart. “You said earlier she wasn’t single. You’re lying, aren’t you?”

Phainon throws the unlit stick on the ground and looks away, crossing her arms as she does so. “I don’t wanna talk about it.”

“Fine, don’t,” Cipher is quick to drop that topic. Out of consideration, or out of lack of interest, Phainon can’t tell. But she’s glad for the diversion. Until Cipher adds, “But just so you know, she texts me every single day at the exact same time to ask the exact same question.”

Phainon can’t help but make a pained face. Because what the hell is she supposed to say to that? “How long?” she opts for the safest reply instead, not wanting to reveal too much. “What do you even say to her?”

Cipher then smiles at her, a smug look on her face, like she’s got her all figured out. Nothing gets past this girl at all. This is why Phainon doesn’t tell her anything. “Wouldn’t you like to know?” she asks her, almost provokingly, but Phainon can’t give her the satisfaction.

“Yes,” Phainon deadpans, not taking her shit. “I wanna know what kind of bullshit you’re feeding her.”

“Girl, relax,” Cipher rolls her eyes. “I just keep telling her the same thing, that you’re doing okay. But wow,” she looks at Phainon with a glint in her eye, as if in amusement. “Way to keep using my place as an excuse, huh? You’ve never even been there.”

The red on Phainon’s cheeks deepened. “I panicked! I couldn’t say Hyacine’s because she sleeps at fucking 10 PM. Honestly, I don’t know how she does that. I can’t sleep unless the clock strikes 1:00 or something.”

Cipher chuckles and leans back onto the wall, now looking ahead of her as she relaxes. “Yeah, and how she doesn’t like partying. I’m glad she still chooses to be friends with us, honestly.”

Phainon then relaxes on the wall too, now that this conversation is finally over. “Yeah. She loves us.”

They stay like that for a few minutes, the comfortable silence engulfing them. 

After a while, Cipher breathes in the fresh air—most likely to savor it before going back to that suffocating mess inside—and then stretches her arms up as she adjusts her posture. “Come on, Phainon. The girls are probably looking for us now.”

Phainon sighs, feeling a headache coming. “Yeah, I know. They can get fussy when drunk, especially Cerydra.”

Cipher huffs and looks at Phainon when her hand reaches the door, immediately understanding the implications. “Tell me about it.”

—

“Are you sure I shouldn’t bring you to your unit? You’re pretty wasted, dude,” Phainon asks Cipher from her motorcycle, when she insists that she walk to the building on her own because her roommate will pick her up from the lobby anyway.

Cipher, unable to form a coherent sentence at that point, only grunts. She smiles at Phainon as she wobbly walks backwards, giving her a thumbs up. “Talk to her,” was all she could muster, her words slurring. 

But Phainon understands very clearly. She winces, but doesn't dignify that with a response. Instead, she says, the volume of her voice turning up as the distance becomes wider, “I’ll see you at Hyacine’s tomorrow.”

“‘Kayyyy.”

With that, Phainon puts on her helmet and drives off, feeling a little too cold, even with the cool air. It’s already 4 AM, which means Mydei could already be awake by now. Titans, why does she have to be such an early bird? It’s a damn Sunday.

When she arrives at their unit, she takes a deep breath as she holds onto the handle, the cold she felt from earlier now condensing as her nerves take over. She bites her lower lip as she finally opens the door, slowly, expecting to see lights from the kitchen. But to her surprise, she was only met with darkness.

Not wanting to disturb the peace, she steps inside slowly, removing her boots right as she closes the door so no footsteps can be heard as she walks in. She removes all her accessories as well and places them inside her bag, not risking it. When it seems like the coast is clear, she heads to the kitchen, longing to be hydrated. She sits on the chair beside the counter as she pours water on a glass, the soles of her feet aching from standing all night on those demonic boots finally getting the rest they deserved.

Titans. That party was a blast. And a disaster. After she and Cipher went back inside the club, the group had scattered around the dance floor. It took the duo about fifteen minutes to assemble the drunken mess of that group, all clearly not in their right minds at that point. Phainon had to call some friends to help send them home, leaving her with Cipher—who downed the last of their drinks because “we paid for these drinks. We are not letting them go to waste.” They most certainly did not pay for those drinks.

As they headed outside—because it was getting too damn late and Cipher’s roommate had been calling her a few times already, most likely out of worry—two men approached the duo. Cipher, with no sense of danger when drunk, paid them no mind. She was still giggling in Phainon’s ear about a joke she already told for the sixth time that night. Phainon, with a mind as sharp as a knife, was already wary, keeping her distance from the two even with a drunken Cipher in tow. She had to put her in front of the motorcycle instead of the back so that she wouldn't fall off. Luckily, Phainon had arms of fucking Elastigirl. Before the men could get near, she was already steering the handles.

As soon as she downs the last of her water, she fishes out her phone to shoot Cipher some texts.

bad kitty 🐈‍⬛ 

4:23 AM

text me when u wake up <

i am worried for ur roommate <

u havent been this drunk before <

i bet u got barf all over her <

She puts the phone down and stretches her arms up, the fatigue getting to her. She’s exhausted, and her eyelids are closing on her, but she knows she can’t be sleeping now when she still got party gunk all over her. Reluctantly, she heads to the bathroom to wash up.

It was a relatively quick shower. She tries to get all the alcohol out, which is hard work in itself, but she doesn’t take more than twenty minutes. Unlike her usual thirty, which used to make Mydei complain a lot. Phainon always thinks she shouldn’t talk when she also takes a while to shower after a jog, or when she returns from the gym. Sometimes she could even catch her setting up the tub. The nerve.

After freshening up, she folds her dirty clothes and places them on the laundry bin. Thank the Titans she’s the one who’s on laundry duty. It’d be embarrassing for her to have Mydei wash all of this… revealing mess.

Mydei knows about Phainon partying. Before the incident , Phainon would tell her every time she goes out to party, and even tells her exactly what time she’d be home. Sometimes twice, but other times it really is just once a month. She never goes out with her party fits though. For some reason, showing Mydei those fits makes her feel dirty. And it’s annoying, because she’s pretty sure Mydei wouldn’t want to be thought of as a prude. She goes to the gym with those fuck ass shorts that shows the underside of her butt, for Titans’ sake.

Phainon, why the fuck are you thinking of my butt just now?

There’s another thing. Whenever she thinks about Mydei or any part of her body, her mind always generates thoughts like these exactly in Mydei’s voice. Any other thought that borders on intrusive that has nothing to do with Mydei, it’s never her voice telling her off. Only when it’s thoughts about Mydei. Seriously. Does Phainon need to seek professional help?

For example, when she cooks a light meal on her own because Mydei isn’t home yet, thoughts about her cooking would always make themselves heard. They’re especially louder and prominent because it’s all Mydei’s voice.

You’re putting too much salt. Why don’t you put paprika? Wuss. I bet you think black pepper is spicy. That’s not enough seasoning. I can make better chicken and broccoli than you. You should just stick to baking. Oh wait, you don’t even know how to do that. Just stick to your salads, then.

What-the fuck-ever. She oughta cook Mydei a full-course dinner one day. That’ll show her.

As she steps out of the bathroom with just a towel wrapped around her, the time reads 4:54 AM. If Mydei wasn’t awake earlier, she might already be now. Phainon looks around, inspecting the kitchen for signs of life—movement, anything.

Except, there are no signs of her around.

It’s a Sunday, anyhow, so Phainon doesn’t feel the need to worry. Maybe Mydei just somehow reviewed a lot last night. Her studying habits are a little… unpredictable.

But for good measure, she tries to knock on the door of her room located just a few feet across hers, putting her… feelings aside. “Mydei?” she calls out quietly, in case she’s still asleep. After a few knocks, and there still isn’t any response from the other side, she decides to let her be, and goes to her own room to change. It’s getting colder, as the heater isn’t on because they agreed to have it off until the end of summer, her short hair already drying up.

The door creaks open, revealing nothing but darkness. The curtains are closed, and Phainon doesn’t remember if she had it like this before leaving. But she doesn’t think too much about it, figuring the fatigue is getting to her. She locks the door behind her and removes her towel, hanging it on the chair next to her desk. She then went to her bedside to open the lamp on the desk, not wanting to have to turn the lights off when she decided to go to sleep.

As she turns on the switch, she is greeted by a big lump on her bed. A suspiciously Mydei-shaped lump, with the same golden-crimson fade hair of the same length and style, and the same curvature of the body…

…the very naked body, in fact. The back is facing Phainon, with red ink marked all over it in suave outlines, painting her body like a mural. She’s never seen her full body tattoo before. It’s mesmerizing. Too mesmerizing, in fact, that she forgot Mydei wasn’t supposed to be there.

That she, too, is naked.

She quickly scrambles across the room to retrieve her towel and wraps it tightly around her body. Titans, imagine if Mydei had to see this.

The girl in question remains unstirred, her body sprawled all over Phainon’s bed like it’s her own. The blanket doesn’t even reach the middle part of her body, revealing her ass— fuck, not again— and the trimmed hairs that trails to the lower part. Fuck. She tries not to inspect her too closely, afraid of stepping out of the line. But she sees something on Mydei’s chest— fuck— like she’s clutching it tight before falling asleep. Wait a fucking minute. Is that…

Is that her sleep dress? HER sleep dress? Her SLEEP dress? Her sleep DRESS? What the fuck?

Mydei is… secretly a pervert?

Mydei? Pervert?

In the same sentence?

This can’t be right. This can’t be the same Mydei she knows. This can’t be the girl who is highly against wearing crop tops. Or the mere concept of lingerie. Because it’s apparently “too unnecessary. At this point, just don’t wear anything at all.”

Oh.

Oh okay.

So that’s what she meant.

Her hand clutching on Phainon’s sleep dress, specifically the pink one where she knows Phainon would wear on Saturday nights because she said she likes looking pretty on Sunday mornings… in passing… once…

Okay, again, what the fuck. Lowkey, this is getting weird.

Highkey, though, this is turning her on a little bit.

But she knows now is not the time for this. She and Mydei haven’t been talking. Hell, none of them had ever made advances on each other. The worst they did was petty flirting, but even then, they don’t go as far as to keep the tension high.

Is this Mydei’s way of communicating, then? Did she know this would finally make Phainon talk? Has she always thought of Phainon as a pervert?

Well she is, a little bit. But that’s not the point.

Holding onto the towel on her chest for dear life—because she knows these things can fall on the worst moments—she walks to the foot of her own bed, narrowing the distance but not enough to get too close. She taps Mydei’s ankle gently, not wanting to deal with an untamed lion when jolted awake.

Unresponsive. She tries again, this time nudging the ankle. Mydei’s soft snore transitioned into a sharp exhale, like the wind was knocked out of her from the nudge. But she still doesn’t wake up.

Has she always been this heavy of a sleeper?

Phainon sighs. She gives up on being careful and removes her towel again now that she knows Mydei won’t stir awake anytime soon, and drops it on the floor. Fuck it. She’ll deal with that mess later. For now, she joins Mydei on the bed, her exhaustion hitting her again like a truck. 

She watches Mydei as she slowly adjusts the blanket, lifting it up so she could slot in her own legs, keeping a respectful distance from Mydei’s. She tries not to avert her eyes to them, no matter how much of a pervert Mydei makes her seem to be. When she finally lies down, she doesn’t turn on her own side, and instead faces Mydei. She gives up on the sleep dress, still somehow tight on Mydei’s hand, and just looks at her instead—how her brows aren’t pulled tightly together, how her mouth is slightly open, showing the front of her teeth (so fucking adorable), and how her hair flows on her body so beautifully. I bet her bed hair would look so majestic.

She quickly pushes away that thought, not wanting to entertain more that could lead to something very inappropriate. She lifted herself up a little so she could turn off the lamp—as she could not sleep with any lights on, no matter how small. When she gets near Mydei’s face, she catches a whiff of an odd scent from her, which she instantly recognizes as alcohol. No fucking wonder.

She then scoffs, thinking about what Mydei could drink herself to that has led to this point. Her face immediately dropped when she thought it could be over them not talking. She dismisses that thought and switches off the light, looking forward to falling unconscious after all this shit that went down. What a fucking night—morning. It’s fucking morning. She turns to her side in frustration and tries to close her eyes.

Only, she can’t sleep.

She squeezes her eyes shut and tries to let herself fall into the sound of the fan whirring, hoping it’ll fade along with her consciousness. Thirty minutes pass, and she still fails, the sound of Mydei’s soft snores drowning out the fan.

Well then, if she’s not going to be able to sleep now, none of them will.

Seeing as none of her previous methods worked, she tries the oldest trick in the book. She reaches out to Mydei’s face, closing her hand into a gesture of pinching, and squeezes Mydei’s nose—blocking all air that could come in. In just a matter of seconds—which was a lot, impressively—Mydei chokes out and slowly blinks awake, to which Phainon lets go, letting her breathe this time.

“Wha…” Mydei stirs, finally conscious. She inspects her surroundings, and then her vision reaches Phainon’s face—her eyes widening in surprise. “What am I doing here?”

“Rise and shine, sweetheart,” Phainon deadpans, resting her elbow on the pillow.

When Mydei’s eyes reach lower, her face reddens, almost matching the ink on her skin. “Oh Titans,” she quickly looks away, embarrassed. “Please tell me you do not sleep naked every night.”

“I don’t,” Phainon tells her straight up, decidingly cannot be embarrassed about this, because she could only imagine how Mydei feels. “You stole my sleep dress.”

Mydei turns to look at her again, this time a little furious. “What? I did not steal your sleep dress.”

Phainon eyes the dress on Mydei’s hand, and looks at her again with a raised eyebrow. When Mydei follows her eyes, she immediately lets go of the dress and palms her eyes, soothing her headache. Yeah, she is so not going to live this down.

“Fuck, I’m sorry,” she hands the dress over to Phainon, who only throws it aside. Mydei looks to where she throws it, but decides to not pay it any mind, not wanting to add onto her headache. “I genuinely don’t know how I got here, nor how I know how THAT got here.”

Now Phainon’s just amused. “Yeah,” she says with a little bit of humor, getting just ready to tease Mydei about it. “I can tell. You reek.”

Mydei groans. “Oh Titans, no wonder.”

“And you’re naked.”

“Stop.”

Phainon snickers. “Were you getting off to me with that dress?”

Mydei hides behind her palms. “I said stop.”

“Seriously,” Phainon reaches out to hold Mydei’s wrist, encouraging her to face her but not quite forcing her to remove her hands. “Have you been doing this before? With my other clothes?”

But Mydei’s hands only tighten on her face. “Shut up.”

“So shameless,” Phainon adds on, again, because she might just be a little too sleep-deprived to realize what she is doing. “You are so perverted, Mydei. I can’t believe you.”

She’s met with silence.

Phainon frowns a little. “Hey,” she taps on Mydei’s wrists. “Are you okay? I was just joking. You know that, right?”

Mydei nods, but doesn’t remove her hands—they only loosen a little.

“Alright. Then can you let go, please? And face me?”

The hands finally slide down as Mydei looks away from Phainon, her eyes red-rimmed. She sniffles and quickly wipes the tear from her eye. Her mouth almost forms into a pout. Phainon finds it endearing that she might just squish her cheeks right there and then.

“Why are you crying, Dei?” Phainon asks softly, deciding to go for the nickname, hoping she’d make Mydei open up.

Mydei glares at her, but the magic seems to work. “You hate me,” she says, her voice cracking.

“What? No I don’t.”

“Stop lying,” she exclaims, sniffling once again. “You refuse to talk to me, you don’t eat dinner with me anymore, you even lie about where you’re going—”

“You knew about that?”

“Of course I do. You’re a shit liar. I already know you go to clubs, so why do you act like you don’t?”

“Mydei, I—”

“No, I don’t wanna hear your excuses. I know I’m probably just a roommate to you, but you’re one of the best friends I ever had, Phai,” the nickname slips out, and Mydei bites on her lower lip at that, but she continues on. “And one day you decided not to talk to me anymore and it got me thinking… do I still know you? Were we ever friends?”

“Of course we are—

“Then why won’t you talk to me? You hurt me, you know. You hurt me and then you worry me to the point of making me text one of your friends everyday even though we’re not close like that. She says you’re fine but I know she’s just covering for you. What is it, Phainon? Am I pestering you? Is that it?”

“No, I—”

“Then what is it?”

“I got jealous!” 

Phainon looks at Mydei in horror and covers her mouth. That’s it. The cat’s finally out of the bag. At 7 fucking AM. Good morning, Phainon. Good morning, Mydei. Oh Kephale, help them.

“No,” Mydei forcibly removes the hand out of Phainon’s mouth. “Do not cover your mouth on me now. What the fuck did you mean by jealous?”

“I…” Phainon sighs and lies back down, feeling faint, her eyes glued to the ceiling. “Remember when you brought someone over?”

Mydei raises her eyebrow. “Yeah?”

“Well, I did not feel good about that.”

“Oh fucking hell,” Mydei slides her hand down her face, feeling frustrated. “I knew it. I knew it and I still didn’t believe it. You’re jealous of my friend? Ms. I-am-friends-with-everyone?”

“It’s different.”

“Literally how is it any different?”

“Because,” Phainon finally faces her again, this time with sadness in her eyes. “I never had anyone over. I thought this was just an exclusive space for us.”

Mydei reaches out to caress Phainon’s face, her own twisting into a soft look, almost as if out of love. “I’m sorry. If it makes you feel better, I never had anyone over again ever since that day.”

Phainon’s eyes widened. “Really?”
